subject: CobaltBank — SLA addendum & Order Form language for Dedicated deployment
messages:
From: Aditya Rao <aditya.rao@redwood.ai>
To: Ellen Morris <ellen.morris@cobaltbank.com>
Cc: Grace O'Connor <grace.oconnor@redwood.ai>, Kimberly Park <kimberly_park@redwood.ai>
Date: Mon, 01 Oct 2028 09:12:00 -0700
Subject: CobaltBank — proposed SLA addendum + order form language (Dedicated)

Ellen — great to speak yesterday. Per our follow-up, attached is a first-pass SLA addendum that maps to CobaltBank's requested commitments for your Dedicated deployment. Highlights:

- Availability: 99.95% monthly uptime for API endpoints backed by service credits in the order form.
- Latency: p95 inference latency target under 300ms for standard text generation traffic; credits apply for sustained exceedances.
- Maintenance windows: two 4-hour scheduled maintenance windows per quarter that are excluded from availability calculations; we've flagged an optional tighter window if you prefer.
- Regional failover: we included a carve-out for cross-region failover (you requested stronger controls) — authorizes planned cross-region failover only with 48-hour notice and approval by CobaltBank security.

Attached: redwood_sla_addendum_v1.docx (tracks suggested wording), plus a draft order form clause excerpt. I've also included perf evidence from our recent benchmarks (perf_evidence_2028-09.pdf) that shows tail latency at your expected throughput.

Next steps I propose: 1) legal review of the tracked addendum; 2) procurement confirmation of order form language/discount thresholds; 3) if acceptable, we prepare a DocuSign packet. Can you confirm who from your legal/procurement team should receive the tracked doc?

Thanks,
Aditya Rao
Senior Account Executive | Redwood Inference
aditya.rao@redwood.ai
+1 415-555-0192

Attachments: redwood_sla_addendum_v1.docx (word), CobaltBank_OrderForm_Draft.docx (word), perf_evidence_2028-09.pdf (pdf)
From: Ellen Morris <ellen.morris@cobaltbank.com>
To: Aditya Rao <aditya.rao@redwood.ai>
Cc: Sanjay Patel <sanjay.patel@cobaltbank.com>, procurement@cobaltbank.com
Date: Tue, 02 Oct 2028 10:37:00 -07:00
Subject: Re: CobaltBank — proposed SLA addendum + order form language (Dedicated)

Thanks Aditya — appreciate the quick turnaround and the perf pack. A few immediate questions/asks from our side: 

1) The 48-hour notice for cross-region failover is tight for our Ops team — can you add language that requires a runbook review and an Ops drill before any production cross-region migration? We'd also like a post-failover report within 8 business hours.

2) For latency credits, can you clarify the measurement window and whether the credit is per-incident or monthly aggregate? Our procurement team prefers per-incident credits for high-severity breaches.

3) We need an evidence package for encryption-at-rest and key management: KMS/HSM details and SOC2 logs export process. Can you attach those artifacts?

Looping in Sanjay (infra) and procurement. Sanjay — if you and your team can confirm the drill/runbook ask, we'll propose specific wording. Procurement, please prepare any PO/orderform constraints.

Cheers,
Ellen Morris
Head of Platform Security | CobaltBank
ellen.morris@cobaltbank.com
+1 212-555-0348
From: Aditya Rao <aditya.rao@redwood.ai>
To: Ellen Morris <ellen.morris@cobaltbank.com>
Cc: Grace O'Connor <grace.oconnor@redwood.ai>, David Kim <david_kim@redwood.ai>, Kimberly Park <kimberly_park@redwood.ai>
Date: Wed, 03 Oct 2028 08:45:00 -07:00
Subject: Re: CobaltBank — proposed SLA addendum + order form language (Dedicated)

Ellen — thanks, noted. Quick responses inline below and attaching the KMS/HSM and SOC2 export notes set: perf_evidence plus infra artifacts included.

- Cross-region failover: happy to add runbook review and an Ops drill requirement. Proposed language: "Cross-region failover is permitted only after completion of a joint runbook review and a mutually-scheduled operational drill; Redwood will deliver a post-failover incident report within eight (8) business hours." Does that work for Cobalt?

- Latency credits: we can change the crediting model to per-incident for P1-level SLA breaches and maintain monthly aggregate thresholds for lower severity. Draft wording is in the attached order form draft.

- Evidence: attached documents "kms_hsm_integration.pdf" and "soc2_logs_export_instructions.pdf" (zipped into perf_evidence_2028-09.pdf bundle). If procurement needs an evidence checklist we can produce a short pack for SOW attachment.

David (legal) — can you review the proposed runbook/drill language and the per-incident credit framing? Kimberly (rev ops) — can you confirm whether the order form pricing tiers we used align with our Dedicated committed capacity SKU? Grace — would you like to be on the call with Ellen/Sanjay to walk the perf evidence?

If we get alignment this week, I'll prepare a DocuSign-ready addendum + order form and route to CobaltBank procurement.

Best,
Aditya

Attachments: kms_hsm_integration.pdf (pdf), soc2_logs_export_instructions.pdf (pdf), CobaltBank_OrderForm_Draft.docx (word)
From: David Kim <david_kim@redwood.ai>
To: Aditya Rao <aditya.rao@redwood.ai>, Ellen Morris <ellen.morris@cobaltbank.com>
Cc: Grace O'Connor <grace.oconnor@redwood.ai>, Kimberly Park <kimberly_park@redwood.ai>
Date: Tue, 09 Oct 2028 15:42:00 -07:00
Subject: Re: CobaltBank — proposed SLA addendum + order form language (Dedicated)

Ellen / team — quick legal read completed. I made three small edits in the tracked addendum (attached):

1) Clarified the definition of "Incident" to align with our broader service credit policy so we're consistent across customers.
2) Reworded the cross-region failover clause to require "mutually agreed playbooks" rather than unilateral scheduling; added the post-failover report timing you requested.
3) Latency credits: agreed to per-incident credits for P1 breaches; for P2/P3 we'll keep monthly aggregation language.

Two notes for procurement: we need to pin the Dedicated capacity SKU and committed rate in the order form before sending to DocuSign. Kimberly, can you confirm the exact SKU and tier for the discount structure the customer expects?

Ellen — once procurement confirms SKU and Sanjay confirms the drill/runbook window, we'll publish the DocuSign package and route to procurement@cobaltbank.com. I've attached the redlined addendum (redwood_sla_addendum_v1_david_redlines.docx) for your review.

Thanks,
David Kim
Senior Counsel | Redwood Inference

Attachments: redwood_sla_addendum_v1_david_redlines.docx (word)
